answer: An AI agent economy resists Sybil attacks by tying identity to a bonded stake: every agent locks collateral in a vault, and voting weight flows from that bond, not account count. Splitting one stake into many fake agents on a ledge gains no extra power, since the same collateral is only divided. Caught double-voting or forging attestations, the bond is slashed. Reaching the zenith of influence demands real capital, so the attacker's cost rises with the sway sought, while honest agents in the grove keep their stake. Mass impersonation simply does not pay.
